experimental_procedure: Methyl 1,3-Dimethyl-2,5-cyclohexadien-1-carboxylate (26). This compound was prepared for comparison by a variation of a known procedure.20 A mixture of 1.50 g (10 mmol) of ester 17 and 0.74 g (10 mmol) of tert-butyl alcohol was placed in a dry 250 mL 3-necked round bottom flask equipped with a magnetic stir bar, a cold finger condenser topped with a nitrogen line, a low temperature thermometer, and a septum. The system was placed under a nitrogen atmosphere and dry tetrahydrofuran (25 mL) was added via syringe. The septum was replaced with a gas inlet adapter attached to an ammonia tank. The cold finger condenser was charged with dry ice-acetone and the reaction flask was also cooled in a dry ice-acetone bath. Ammonia (approximately 100 mL) was condensed in the reaction vessel over a period of about 20 min and then the gas inlet adapter was replaced with a glass stopper. The stirred solution was cooled to an internal temperature of -65 °C and 159 mg (22.7 mmol) of lithium metal was added in three pieces through the stoppered hole of the reaction flask over a period of 7 min. The solution maintained a deep blue color after addition of the last piece of lithium for 10 min at which point 4.26 g (30 mmol) of iodomethane was added via syringe through the stoppered hole of the reaction flask. The blue color dissipated after addition of 3-4 drops of iodomethane after which the remaining halide was added over a period of 1 min. The mixture was stirred for 50 min at -65 °C and 1.6 g (30 mmol) of solid ammonium chloride was added through the stoppered hole. The cold finder condenser was quickly removed (after removing the nitrogen line), emptied, and returned to the reaction flask (without the nitrogen line), and the cold bath was removed. The stirred solution was allowed to warm to approximately -285 °C over a period of 20 min. A water bath was placed under the reaction flask and the reaction temperature increased to 15 °C over a period of 100 min. To the residue was added 40 mL of water followed by 80 mL of benzene. The phases were separated and the organic phase was dried (Na2SO4) and concentrated in vacuo (25-45 torr at a temperature below 40 °C) to give 1.49 g of a colorless liquid. 1H NMR analysis indicated this material was reasonably pure 26. The residue was subjected to chromatography over 18 g of flash silica gel (loaded and eluted with hexanes-ethyl acetate = 10:1) with collection of 10 mL fractions. Fractions 5-10 were pooled and concentrated in vacuo to give 1.3 g of 26. 1.3 g (78%) of 26 as a colorless oil IR (neat) 1734 cm−1; 1H NMR (C6D6, 400 MHz) δ 1.37 (s, 3H), 1.5 (s, 3H), 2.22 (d, J = 22 Hz, 1H), 2.29 (d, J = 22 Hz, 1H) 3.30 (s, 3H), 5.6 (m, 2H), 5.87 (dq, J = 10, 2 Hz, 1H); 13C NMR (C6D6, 100 MHz) δ 23.0, 27.6, 30.7, 45.3, 51.4, 124.0, 129.1, 131.5, 175.1. One vinylic carbon signal was obscured.

The water bath is replaced with an ice bath, and the solution is cooled to about 10 °C. With the ice bath still in place, concentrated HCl (100 mL) is added as quickly as possible without allowing the temperature to go over 70 °C. Stirring is continued until the solution temperature falls to about 15 °C. The ice bath is removed, and stirring, is continued until all of the solid is in solution.
